instruction: Explain what a Git merge conflict is and how to resolve one.
response_a:
A git merge conflict occurs when two different versions of the same file have been merged into your local repository simultaneously. This can happen if you're working on multiple branches or features in parallel with each other without merging them all at once (known as "feature-branch" merges). When this happens, there's no clear winner for which version should be committed first - it depends upon personal preference but also based on whether certain changes were made last time they happened before being pushed back up through history again. 

To solve these conflicts:

1) Check out both files side by side using `git diff`. 

2) Identify where lines from either branch differ between commits that need resolving. You'll likely see some kind of line number next to those differences indicating their position within commit messages.

3) Use an editor like vim or nano to navigate around the problematic areas looking for any conflicting text such as comments/comments etc., then use grep command followed by 'diff' commands together to find matching lines across both files.

4) Once found, make sure only valid parts of code match so don't add anything else until after making necessary corrections. If not, revert previous change(s), otherwise continue editing whatever needs fixing.
